**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict the bcrypt byte cap to local identities**

Once a migrated user resets their password in Firebase, or a Firebase-native account is created, with a valid password over 72 UTF-8 bytes, this early return rejects the credential without contacting Firebase. The 72-byte cap is specific to local bcrypt hashing, while [Firebase password policies support passwords up to 4,096 characters](https://firebase.google.com/docs/auth/web/password-auth), so a credential accepted by the authoritative provider can become unusable through this adapter; apply this check only to `local` identities or enforce an equivalent provider-side policy.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in fc997b45558c7f3ca610e947e800c9424f43b5ce. The 72-byte cap now applies only to local bcrypt identities. A synthetic regression verifies a 120-byte Unicode Firebase password reaches the provider unchanged and authenticates, while local oversized credentials remain rejected. Real Firebase policy/sign-in rehearsal is still explicitly unexecuted.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Persist verified user changes immediately**

This persists the workspace only after a tracked query succeeds, so `updateCurrentUser` changes can remain absent from the snapshot indefinitely. For example, `legal-update.tsx` updates `account_access` without refreshing any allowlisted tracking query; if connectivity then fails and the app reloads, restoration uses the old `legal_acceptance_required` user and the tab layout redirects away from local tracking. Persist identity changes directly in `updateCurrentUser` in both auth implementations rather than relying on an unrelated query event.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enter reconnection mode for every retryable failure**

When an established session receives a retryable 408/429/500/502 response, this leaves `pendingReconnection` false because only status 503 is recognized; API-client-generated request timeouts are also raised outside this `fetchImpl` and never reach its catch handler. Consequently an outage can leave no reconnection status or explicit retry loop, and each subsequent edit continues contacting the unhealthy server before it is queued. Apply the shared retryability classification to completed API failures and timeouts in both browser and native clients, rather than special-casing one status here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 62cfa5f755a9737f0e6fa66e064e381ff4a4cac7. Both updateCurrentUser paths now persist same-account verified user changes immediately. Browser/native regressions update account_access without any following query event and restore the updated snapshot.

Fixed in 62cfa5f755a9737f0e6fa66e064e381ff4a4cac7. A completed-request API error observer now receives parsed HTTP errors and client-generated timeouts. Both auth providers use the shared retryability classifier and retain identity while entering reconnection mode. Tests cover 408/429/500/502/503, a transport that ignores abort, and established-session continuity. Caller cancellation and explicit non-retryable envelopes retain their existing semantics.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Project queued mutations into the local workspace**

When the device is offline, this path durably queues the mutation but does not update the cached tracking data that is displayed and persisted by `saveOfflineWorkspace`. For example, `WeightEntrySheet` reports “Saved on this device” and merely invalidates `mobile-metrics`; because requests remain blocked until reconnection, Today and a subsequent offline reload still show the old weight. Food additions and edits have the same stale-view behavior, preventing users from reviewing or correcting what they just logged locally. Apply queued operations optimistically to the relevant query data (and snapshot it), or otherwise materialize the outbox state in tracking views.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed using the suggested alternative of materializing durable outbox state in tracking views. Review saved changes now shows exact persisted weight/date, food creation/edit quantities, and deletion/day intent after offline restart, without inventing server IDs or authoritative totals. Cached totals are explicitly last-synchronized. Same-date weight corrections replay in order; editing newly queued food rows remains unavailable until sync and is disclosed. Two real-browser outage/offline-reload cases verify the saved value remains reviewable and disappears after a single verified replay; four focused presentation regressions cover weight, food creation/edit, zero values, and field allowlisting. Please assess this explicit pending-state representation rather than optimistic server-cache mutation.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the last cache until tracking data reloads**

On every cold start where `/auth/me` succeeds, the query client is still empty when this unconditional save runs, so it replaces the previous offline snapshot with an identity-only snapshot. If the tracking endpoints then return a retryable error, or connectivity drops before the first tracking query succeeds, the prior food and weight cache is already gone and the next offline reload has no tracking data to restore. Hydrate the verified same-account snapshot before replacing it, or defer replacement until a tracked query has succeeded; the native `persistAuthPayload` path has the same ordering issue.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Superseding the earlier review-sheet-only disposition: 8e227d6b now projects durable ordered intent directly into Today, food logs, weight entry and Progress. Local food add/repeated edit/delete and weight correction/delete remain visible after restart. Immutable creation requests/operation IDs recover real server receipts for dependent writes; acknowledged rows are persisted before dequeue, and receipt identities prevent duplicate overlays after a pre-dequeue crash. Browser regressions execute food add/edit twice/reload/delete/reload/reconnect with exactly one creation, two edits and one deletion, plus offline weight correction/deletion. Scoped hooks reject other-account/server intent; pure regressions cover partial replay and rejected receipt recovery.

Fixed in 8e227d6b. Verified same-account snapshots hydrate before accepting the authenticated user, with an async generation guard. Saving an empty or partially loaded cache retains existing allowlisted queries for that exact origin/user, while newer authoritative query snapshots replace their own keys. Browser regression now queues a weight, performs a successful cold auth while tracking/replay endpoints fail, then reloads into an auth outage and verifies cached food and the projected weight remain. Account mismatch and departed-generation hydration are covered separately.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Limit food-query blocking to relevant active mutations**

When any food mutation exists in the outbox, this disables fetching for every `mobile-food` date, including mutations whose state is `failed`. For example, a rejected edit for today remains a durable queue barrier, so navigating to yesterday or refreshing after another device changed it can only show the cached value (or an empty list) until that failed mutation is resolved. Restrict blocking to active mutations relevant to this date, or allow the server snapshot to refresh and overlay the queued intent.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed by restricting holds to active, date-relevant intent (including cached-ID matching for legacy edits). Failed mutations no longer block food or metric refresh. New edit/delete payloads retain their date. Background prefetch uses the same active-date check, and refreshed rows retain known immutable receipt identities so an acknowledged creation does not duplicate its local overlay. Hook regressions verify unrelated-date loading and successful refresh through a failed edit while preserving pending intent; receipt regression verifies deduplication after server refresh. Offline Add food is also asserted fully inside the viewport.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Queue day-state changes behind existing tracking writes**

When the outbox already contains a food mutation but authentication is currently healthy, this sends the day-status change directly instead of preserving queue order. For example, completing a day before its queued food creation replays closes the day on the server; the later creation then receives the backend's non-retryable `FOOD_DAY_NOT_OPEN` response and becomes a permanent queue barrier. Pass the existing-mutation state through `forceQueue`, as the food and weight mutation paths do, so day completion, pause, and resume operations cannot overtake pending tracking writes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let corrections replace failed queued mutations**

If a queued local creation has already failed permanently, editing its projected row adds this update after the failed mutation because `outbox.mutations.length` remains nonzero. `SqliteOutbox.claimNext()` treats that oldest failed row as a barrier, so the correction is never replayed, while retrying only resubmits the unchanged failed creation. This occurs, for example, when an offline saved-food creation later gets `My food not found`; changing its displayed values cannot recover synchronization. Replace or discard the failed intent when correcting it rather than appending an unreachable update.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in the current head: all day completion, pause, resume and pause-extension mutations force queueing behind existing outbox intent. A healthy-auth regression proves day completion cannot overtake a food creation.

Fixed with explicit selective discard instead of automatic request replacement. A failed creation may also represent a local receipt-persistence failure after server success; silently assigning a new operation ID could duplicate food. The editor now prevents unreachable corrections and offers retry guidance or a confirmed atomic discard of only the failed creation and its dependent edits. Other account/server queues and independent writes remain intact; a concurrent retry invalidates discard. Exported-browser recovery, real IndexedDB transaction tests and SQLite transaction tests pass. The user can then add a corrected entry; no server record is implicitly deleted.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply failed-create deletion handling to the content card**

When a failed local creation is projected, `foodState` is non-empty, so `AsyncStateBoundary` renders its children and never uses this new `empty` callback; the rendered card still sends deletion directly to `deleteRecovery.requestDelete`. Deleting that row therefore queues a `food.delete` behind the permanently failed creation, hides the row, and leaves the queue barrier in place while making the per-entry discard flow inaccessible. Use the failed-creation-aware handler for the content card as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed at 86c902330964ad9fb77c6938d53d26fde4c557f6: both empty and populated cards use one failed-creation-aware requestDelete handler. The exported-browser regression now enters the recovery sheet through Delete on the actual populated failed row, confirms selective discard, and verifies removal after restart. All four maintained offline browser scenarios passed at this head; typecheck passed.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bypass the local-only gate when logging out**

After any retryable API failure sets `localOnlyRef`, this gate also rejects the explicit `logoutBrowser()` request. If the server recovers and the user logs out before the reconnection loop clears the flag, `logout` still clears local state in its `finally` block but never invalidates the persistent HttpOnly cookie; reloading then calls `/auth/me` with that cookie and signs the user back in. Send logout through an ungated client so the cookie-backed session is actually terminated.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L13-L16](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/86c902330964ad9fb77c6938d53d26fde4c557f6/AGENTS.md#L13-L16)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 2ccff558633c9fd743162687bc404cfc2d81822d: durable explicit sign-out suppresses restoration, ungated revocation retries after outages, and new login waits for revocation. Native late refresh/token-storage races are covered. Six synthetic HTTPS browser scenarios and 1,107 mobile tests passed; no physical-device or live Firebase claim.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revoke the server session despite cleanup failures**

If local cleanup rejects—for example, the newly covered `clearOnboardingDraft` failure—this `await` aborts logout before `flushExplicitLogout` runs, so the UI signs out but the HttpOnly cookie session remains valid on an otherwise reachable server. The retry hook does not immediately flush while the tab is already online and foregrounded, so revocation may wait until a later foreground/reload; run cleanup and revocation independently so local storage failures cannot suppress server sign-out. The native logout has the same sequencing issue.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L13-L16](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/2ccff558633c9fd743162687bc404cfc2d81822d/AGENTS.md#L13-L16)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in e807e9e872e0fe00279bb3c437bc3eb23aa6de52. Browser and native logout now invoke revocation in finally even when local cleanup rejects. Focused regressions force onboarding-draft cleanup failure and assert server logout; native also proves pending credential material is erased after acknowledgement. 34 focused auth/storage tests and typecheck pass. Captured successful-cleanup UI is unaffected; source applicability remains explicit.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle failed edits before accepting corrections**

When an earlier queued `food.update` receives a non-retryable response, such as a server-side validation rejection, the projected cached row remains editable, but this guard only recognizes a failed parent `food.create`. Saving a corrected value therefore appends another update because `forceQueue` sees the existing mutation; `claimNext()` continues to stop at the older failed update, so the correction can never synchronize and the UI still reports success. Fresh evidence in the current head is that `failedCreation` is derived exclusively from `localCreation.operationId`, leaving failed updates on ordinary server rows unhandled; detect failed mutations targeting the edited row and offer replacement/discard recovery or block the save.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 503670b85cbb95f83c6598753a867e75b92800c8. Failed creation/update/delete share explicit recovery: retry the unchanged original request or confirm atomic discard of only the selected entry queued food intent, never silent changed-payload replay. Save and Delete cannot append unreachable corrections while the entry has failed intent; queued deletion behind a failed edit no longer hides recovery. Existing rows and optimistic creation references are covered, with multiple edits, retry/discard races, dates/accounts and unrelated work. Seven exported-browser scenarios and 221 mobile suites/1114 tests passed; an additional projection assertion passed. Capture/body reconciliation is underway; no readiness claim.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replace the non-ASCII settings separator**

When the failed-creation alert is rendered, this text introduces a Unicode arrow into a UI string; use an ASCII separator such as `Settings > Offline changes` to keep the client copy consistent with the repository's punctuation convention.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L218-L221](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/503670b85cbb95f83c6598753a867e75b92800c8/AGENTS.md#L218-L221)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Extract the discard-button label mapping**

Move this four-way `confirmDiscard`/`failedCreation` label selection into a named variable or helper instead of nesting ternaries in JSX; the current expression makes the recovery-state labels unnecessarily difficult to verify and directly violates the repository's documented UI mapping convention.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L229-L232](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/503670b85cbb95f83c6598753a867e75b92800c8/AGENTS.md#L229-L232)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 184021ee3d9780162580fd845c1a54869892dd7e: failed-creation guidance now uses Settings > Offline changes, matching AGENTS.md ASCII punctuation guidance. Both affected browser recovery scenarios pass from the committed export.

Fixed in 184021ee3d9780162580fd845c1a54869892dd7e: named discardLabels mapping and discardButtonLabel replace nested JSX ternaries, preserving all four existing labels. Typecheck, 28 focused tests and both affected browser recovery scenarios passed.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve failed weight writes before queuing replacements**

When a queued `metric.add` or `metric.delete` receives a non-retryable response, it remains as the failed head of the outbox, but the projected weight stays editable. This `forceQueue` path then reports a corrected save or repeated deletion as queued behind that failure; `claimNext()` will never reach it, and unlike food mutations there is no selective failed-weight discard path (the settings UI can only retry the unchanged request). The failed weight therefore blocks the correction and every later queued mutation indefinitely, so detect failed metric intent and offer recovery or block the replacement save.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed at afa5dc7669251b4a0bee6c093f677048dd2af45e. Both stores reject related correction enqueue atomically behind a permanent failure, and weight Save/Delete show explicit retry/scoped discard. The audit covers all ten kinds through an exhaustive shared policy; food uses entry identity, weight uses calendar date (legacy unknown dates fail conservatively), and tracking controls require confirmation of their listed group. Scoped discard preserves unrelated dates/accounts and immediately attempts remaining replay. Synthetic unit/provider suites and actual browser add/delete failure scenarios passed before integration; combined-master checks and refreshed evidence are being completed. No server rollback or live Firebase action is implied.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Serialize the direct-write decision with the outbox**

Fresh evidence beyond the earlier queue-order fix is that `mutations` is provider-local React state and the browser provider has no cross-tab change subscription. If another open tab queues a food creation after this tab's last refresh, this value remains empty and a day completion is sent directly, allowing it to close the day ahead of the durable creation; replay then fails with `FOOD_DAY_NOT_OPEN`. Consult or lock the durable outbox when deciding between direct execution and enqueueing, rather than relying only on the current component snapshot.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Continue logout when intent persistence fails**

Fresh evidence after the cleanup-failure fix is that `beginExplicitLogout` itself remains outside the `try`: if its AsyncStorage write rejects because browser storage is blocked, unavailable, or full, logout exits before either `clearSession` or `flushExplicitLogout`, leaving both the UI session and HttpOnly cookie authenticated. Attempt local cleanup and server revocation independently even when the durable intent cannot be written; the native logout has the same sequencing issue.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L15-L15](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/afa5dc7669251b4a0bee6c093f677048dd2af45e/AGENTS.md#L15-L15)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed at ed170e7e8a716e6a1b71b726bb49a0a184c01ad6. Every supported tracking producer now uses a namespace dispatch lock, reads the durable outbox inside it and keeps the direct attempt/enqueue decision serialized. Browser Web Locks coordinate tabs; unsupported browsers queue instead of sending unordered direct writes. Native dispatch is serialized within the runtime. Eligible new enqueue requests replay without altering unchanged deferred backoff. A real two-tab browser regression starts the first tab with an empty snapshot, queues food in the other tab, verifies completion remains behind it in IndexedDB and observes food then completion after reconnection. Shared concurrency tests cover competing dispatch, account isolation and stale bindings.

Fixed at ed170e7e8a716e6a1b71b726bb49a0a184c01ad6. beginExplicitLogout persistence rejection no longer prevents local cleanup or revocation. The store preserves unsaved intent in process, retains native token material only in native memory, and never overwrites an unreadable durable record. Post-revocation storage failure does not suppress successful revocation. If both storage and networking fail, the signed-out UI explicitly warns that revocation is pending and the app must stay open until reconnection. Browser/native auth and store regressions pass; actual browser tests verify storage rejection still revokes, and simultaneous storage/503 failure displays the warning then completes memory-held revocation after a real offline-to-online transition. No restart durability is claimed without usable storage.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Hold the reopen and dependent food write under one lock**

When adding food to a completed day and the reopen is queued, `executeOrQueueMutation` releases the namespace dispatch lock before this second `enqueue` acquires it. Another tab can enqueue a day completion in that gap, producing `reopen -> completion -> food.create`; replay then closes the day before creating the food and leaves the creation permanently failed with `FOOD_DAY_NOT_OPEN`. Fresh evidence after the dispatch-lock fix is this two-step producer spanning two separate lock acquisitions, so enqueue the reopen and its dependent creation atomically under one dispatch lock.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 7ff6937c9cd43fea1e239b537b6f77adfcbf1dda. AddFoodSheet now holds one namespace dispatch lock across reopening and the dependent food write, including retryable queued fallback. The maintained concurrency regression fails against exact prior ed170e7e (OPEN, COMPLETE, food.create) and passes fixed code (OPEN, food.create, COMPLETE); all18 focused tests and mobile typecheck pass. Existing calendar browser reopening/edit/completion scenario passes. The concurrency proof is component-level; no unsupported browser concurrency claim.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recheck queued day state before skipping reopen**

When another browser tab has already queued a completion for this date, this tab can still hold a stale cached `OPEN` day. The dispatch correctly sees the durable row and sets `mustQueue`, but this condition skips the reopen and queues only `food.create`, producing `COMPLETE -> food.create`; replay then receives the backend's non-retryable `FOOD_DAY_NOT_OPEN` response and leaves a permanent queue barrier. Unlike the fixed `reopen -> completion -> food.create` gap, the new compound callback must also account for preceding day-status intent under the lock before deciding that no reopen is required.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in b1495731a13105b9067936ff8ae4c3b2763671bb. The locked dispatch callback receives the ordered durable queue and applies same-date food-day.set-status and legacy food-day.update intent before deciding whether to reopen. A queued PAUSED day blocks submission. Both completion regressions fail against exact7ff6937c (COMPLETE,food.create) and pass fixed code (COMPLETE,OPEN,food.create).40 focused tests and mobile typecheck pass; final full-suite/export and configured CI/review are running. No prior feedback was waived.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize the real queued pause operation**

When another tab queues a pause for this day while this tab still caches `OPEN`, the durable row is `food-tracking-pause.start` with `starts_on`, not `food-day.set-status` with `date: ... status: 'PAUSED'`. This filter therefore ignores the pause, then queues `food.create` behind it; replay materializes the day as paused and the food write fails permanently with `FOOD_DAY_NOT_OPEN`. The added PAUSED regression uses a row that the API and replay executor do not permit, so update the ordered-state calculation to account for actual pause/resume operations.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed by shared invariant82d916b6. Ordered durable projection recognizes actual food-tracking-pause.start(starts_on) and resume(resumed_on), preserves earlier paused dates, and rejects failed relevant controls. The component pause regression now uses the real start operation. All food.create/update/delete dispatch plus both transactional store insertion paths share the closed-day guard; edits/deletes/barcode never silently reopen. Add Food retains explicit submit-to-reopen under one lock. Matrix covers repeated two-producer operations and persisted restart/replay.225 suites/1178 tests pass; current browser/CI/review pending.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve replayed day state for stale dispatchers**

In the browser cross-tab flow, this derives the effective status only from rows still in IndexedDB. Once another tab successfully replays a queued completion or pause, `OutboxReconciler` deletes that row at `mobile/src/offline/reconciler.ts:83-85`, while this tab's cached day can remain stale as `OPEN` because there is no cross-tab cache invalidation. If this tab is offline, or its direct food request encounters a retryable failure, it can therefore queue a food mutation without the required reopen/resume; replay later reaches the server's closed day and leaves a permanent `FOOD_DAY_NOT_OPEN` failure. Preserve or broadcast applied control state, or coordinate replay completion with dispatch so deleting the row cannot erase the only authoritative ordering evidence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in 856cc30b0d28e6d8510244c984dc4c5e36959f89. Successful day/pause/resume controls now persist account/server-scoped receipts before replay removes queued rows. Stale dispatch reads acknowledged receipts plus pending intent under the namespace lock; offline startup projects them, while fresh authoritative day reads reconcile them under that same lock. Create/edit/delete stay guarded after queue deletion and persisted reopen; no background reopen is manufactured. Receipt-write failure retains the original control request identity. Added completion/pause restart, account-isolation, slow-read/newer-completion and persistence-failure regressions. Also fixed an observed real two-tab replay race: interruption recovery and replay now share namespace ownership with dispatch; startup no longer reclaims another tab outside the lock.227 suites/1184 tests, typecheck, Knip and export pass; final browser/CI/review running.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve newer state when replaying an acknowledged control**

If a day/pause request committed but the client was interrupted before dequeuing it, another client can subsequently change that state before recovery. Replaying the original operation ID then returns the backend's cached response without reapplying the old mutation, but this line records the old queued payload as the newest local receipt anyway. Because replay does not necessarily refetch that day, an old completion or pause can overwrite a newer authoritative OPEN/resumed state and incorrectly block offline food logging; avoid advancing the receipt from an idempotent replay when newer authoritative state may already have been observed, or reconcile it with a post-replay server read.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 472b2a1600fc3be122d3bdebbb380b3adc11a8a8. Control replay now treats the cached idempotency response only as proof of acceptance, then reads current server day/pause state before updating cache/receipts or deleting the queued row. It never promotes the old queued completion/pause/resume payload to newest local state. A failed verification read leaves the original request pending. Regressions simulate a server commit plus lost response, an intervening second-client reopen/resume, then cached replay: one server write, unchanged original ID, final OPEN preserved. An older resume also cannot overwrite a newer paused-day receipt. Exact856cc30 executor/reconciler fail the two lost-response cases; fixed source passes.51 focused tests, typecheck and Knip pass; exact-head full mobile/build/browser/CI are completing. PR426 overlap was reported in issue421 comment6004499444; no other branch was changed.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return current state when replaying pause updates**

When an offline `food-tracking-pause.update` is replayed, its executor branch still returns `void`, so this new check throws after `updateFoodTrackingPause` has already succeeded. The ordinary `Error` is classified as non-retryable, leaving the successfully applied mutation marked failed at the head of the outbox and blocking every later saved change; either exclude expectation-only updates from this requirement or make that branch read and return the current pause state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record the verified resume boundary before dequeueing**

When a queued resume is replayed and remains the current server state, `getFoodTrackingPause()` returns the inactive all-null object, so this records only an `OPEN` receipt for the exact resumed day and never records a resume boundary. Any earlier persisted pause-start receipt therefore continues to project every later date as `PAUSED` after the pending resume row is removed, causing stale/offline clients to reject food logging on subsequent days; the verified inactive state must supersede that prior pause timeline before dequeueing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in 709f4545: pause.update now verifies and returns current pause state after successful mutation, including an empty response body; it no longer becomes a failed barrier. The maintained all-control matrix covers completion/reopen/legacy updates/pause/update/resume, verification outage, original-ID retry, intervening server state and storage restart. Full mobile suite:227 suites/1197 tests passed.

Addressed in 709f4545: a fresh pause snapshot atomically replaces obsolete pause-derived receipts before dequeueing. Inactive state removes stale indefinite pause projections without inventing a resume date from a cached response; active state preserves the newer server pause. Separately verified exact-day COMPLETE/PAUSED observations survive. Maintained regressions cover later dates after resume, restart and an intervening active pause; prior472 source fails five new checks.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop automatically retrying failed mutations**

When a mutation has been classified as non-retryable and stored as `failed`, a connectivity or foreground transition still calls `replay(true)`, which invokes `reconciler.retryFailed()` without an ID in `provider.web.tsx:238-242` and `provider.tsx:190-194`, resetting every failed row to pending.
